Effects of household, agricultural and metal water pollutants.
keyPoints: ["Household waste can add pathogens and detergents.","Agricultural runoff can add nutrients and pesticides.","Toxic metals can accumulate and harm health."]
modelAnswer: Household wastes such as detergents, paints, oils, food waste, and sewage can make water unfit for aquatic life and spread disease. Agricultural wastes and runoff add fertilizers, nitrates, phosphates, pesticides, and animal waste; these can cause eutrophication and oxygen depletion. Toxic metal compounds can accumulate in aquatic organisms and harm humans who consume them.

stem: How do house hold wastes, agricultural wastes and metals affect living organisms as water pollutants?
keyPoints: ["Household and agricultural wastes contaminate water.","Metals can be toxic and bioaccumulate.","Pollution harms aquatic life and human health."]
modelAnswer: Household wastes introduce sewage, pathogens, detergents, paints, oils, and food waste. Agricultural wastes and runoff introduce fertilizers, nitrates, phosphates, pesticides, and livestock waste. Toxic metals can poison aquatic organisms, accumulate through food chains, and harm human health. These pollutants can reduce dissolved oxygen, kill aquatic life, and spread waterborne disease.
